claim: Evaluate+commit has no cost
technical_note: Atomic commit approximately doubles p50 on largest G64 batch.

claim: Verified-event compaction can reduce output memory by observed yield
source_basis: Physical GPU report and subgroup compact runs
technical_note: Subgroup/workgroup compact E16 output was validated and timed; 4.7488% yield produced a 21.058x logical output-stream reduction, while a zero-overflow 6.25%-capacity FIFO produced a measured 16x output-allocation reduction at N=4194304.

claim: A one-fetch confidence LUT is necessarily faster than direct exp2 or the smaller two-fetch LUT
source_basis: Physical GPU report and balanced LUT-pair runs
technical_note: The 16 KiB interval-pair LUT removed one dynamic texture fetch and improved some small/mid-size cases, but did not provide a stable end-to-end advantage; direct exp2 remains the recommended path for this exact kernel.

claim: Pre-thresholding the monotonic confidence predicate provides a universal material speedup
source_basis: Physical GPU report and balanced pre-threshold runs
technical_note: It moved exp2 to verified lanes and improved append-only paired medians by 1.0-4.5% at smaller/mid sizes, but converged to +0.03% at N=4194304 and gave no consistent counted-path advantage.

claim: A 128-byte log-threshold LUT is the cause of the G24 hot-state speedup
source_basis: Physical GPU report and balanced G24 control/boundary runs
technical_note: The same-layout direct decoder was faster below L2 and tied the LUT when bandwidth-bound; the 24-byte record reduced state-plus-output allocation 1.32x, measured 1.306x append and 1.312x counted speedups at N=4194304, and displaced the narrow residency cliff by the expected footprint ratio.

claim: Splitting lineage into a cold stream makes the total state record 20 bytes
source_basis: Physical GPU yield/compression report and isolated balanced cold-lineage runs
technical_note: The hot geometry/meta stride is 20 bytes but a separate 4-byte lineage value remains allocated per candidate, so total state storage stays 24 bytes. At N=4194304 the split measured 1.108x append and 1.110x counted throughput versus G24 because only verified lanes logically load lineage; exact cache-sector traffic remains unmeasured.

claim: The measured G20 append gain comes from lower register or shared-memory use
source_basis: Native pipeline-executable statistics in the isolated cold-lineage aggregate
technical_note: The NVIDIA driver reports 22 registers, 2052 bytes shared memory and a 3456-byte executable for both G24 and G20 append kernels across all six captures. The timing difference is therefore consistent with locality/traffic rather than lower reported compute-resource use.

claim: Putting a packed LUT behind the texture-buffer path provides an additional effective cache-capacity tier
source_basis: Physical GPU report and balanced byte-identical texture/SSBO controls
technical_note: Random texture/SSBO throughput ratios are 0.989x, 1.002x, 1.000x and 1.000x at 16, 32, 64 and 128 MiB. Both paths lose about 79.36% from 32 to 64 MiB, so texelFetch does not bypass the shared lower cache/memory bottleneck for this workload.

claim: The native dependent-load sweep locates an effective random working-set transition immediately above the reported 36 MiB L2 capacity
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH OBSERVABILITY BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four isolated shader-clock runs
technical_note: Random control-subtracted time is flat through 36 MiB, rises 1.242x at 38 MiB and 2.134x at 40 MiB, and reaches 4.714x at 64 MiB relative to 36 MiB. VK_KHR_shader_clock units are implementation-defined and 65536 in-flight chains expose scheduling, so these values are not labelled hardware cycles, nanoseconds, raw single-load latency, or cache-hit rate.

claim: The native L2/global dependent path has a measured cycle-domain hot-versus-post-eviction cost on the named GPU
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH WARP-EXPOSURE BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four isolated CUDA clock64 runs
technical_note: Native sm_120 SASS uses CS2R SR_CLOCKLO and LDG.E.STRONG.GPU with zero spills. Across 4-128 MiB tables, immediate-hot dependent warp steps measure 399.569 cycles and post-256-MiB-eviction steps measure 1087.789 cycles at the median of size medians, a 2.722x ratio. clock64 includes time slicing and each warp step can service 32 random sectors, so this is not scalar transaction latency.

claim: Keeping the concurrent random hot working set at or below the named GPU's reported L2 capacity preserves materially higher requested-load throughput
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH LOGICAL-THROUGHPUT BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four isolated CUDA concurrency runs
technical_note: At the occupancy-query ceiling of 1104 independent warps, immediate-hot requested throughput is 43.215 Gload/s at 36 MiB and 23.683 Gload/s at 40 MiB, a 45.20% drop immediately beyond nominal L2; 64 and 128 MiB reach 9.357 and 7.524 Gload/s. All 240 raw rows and 74,678,400 payloads validate. Gload/s counts logical u32 requests rather than physical cache sectors or DRAM transactions.

claim: A native texture-object path gives the packed random dependent LUT additional effective cache capacity beyond the L2/global path
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four isolated CUDA texture/global runs
technical_note: Native SASS uses TLD.LZ for texture and LDG.E.STRONG.GPU for global. At full occupancy their median hot-rate ratio across 4-128 MiB is 0.99949x; from 36 to 40 MiB global loses 45.159% and texture loses 45.246%. At one warp texture is 13.65% slower. All 256 raw rows and 98,426,880 payloads validate.

claim: Dense 6-bit log-code packing realizes the calculated 2.667x cache-resident capacity increase with near-slot throughput on the native texture path
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH LOGICAL-THROUGHPUT BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four isolated CUDA packed-log-LUT runs
technical_note: At full occupancy slot16 holds 18,874,368 codes in 36 MiB at 43.192 Glookup/s through TLD; packed6 holds 50,331,648 codes in the same bytes at 42.594 Glookup/s, exactly 2.667x capacity for a 1.39% rate loss. The packed texture path falls 45.05% at 40 MiB, retaining the shared L2 boundary. All 704 raw rows and 270,673,920 payloads validate, including 92,390,031,360 per-load code checks. Glookup/s is logical and hardware counters remain unavailable.

claim: Strictly dependent isolated random u32 pointers consume an effective 128-byte L2 residency unit on the named workload
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH WORKLOAD AND PHYSICAL-LINE BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and eight isolated CUDA sparse-stride runs
technical_note: At full occupancy the approximately 43.0 Gload/s hot plateau holds 1,179,648 nodes at 32-byte spacing, 589,824 at 64 bytes and 294,912 at 128 or 256 bytes, a 4:2:1 capacity ratio. The 256-byte allocation tracks the 128-byte rate curve despite 2x allocation, while the 589,824-node 128-byte case reaches only 0.3296x of the hot anchor and rejects a 64-byte model. All 1,448 rows validate and the complete measured kernels execute 366,678,638,592 dependent loads. This is specific to the dependent pointer chase and is not a universal per-code charge or counter-derived physical cache line/sector size.

claim: The dependent pointer chase's 128-byte effective residency is a universal per-code cost for independently scheduled packed-LUT lookups
source_basis: Physical GPU report and eight isolated CUDA packed-LUT line-occupancy runs
technical_note: With one useful code in each aligned 128-byte region, a 40 MiB allocation retains 99.02% of its 28 MiB texture rate instead of cliffing immediately above the reported 36 MiB L2. Across 1-170 useful codes, 36 MiB sustains 42.437-43.010 Glookup/s while 40 MiB changes progressively with the exact probability of touching each 32-byte address region. All 1,792 rows validate and the timed kernels execute 453,790,138,368 code lookups. Address spans are arithmetic, not counter-measured hardware sectors.

claim: Independent sparse packed-LUT throughput requires separate resident-data containing-line-address and address-span terms
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH MODEL AND COUNTER BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report plus eight sparse-address runs and four one-code refinement runs
technical_note: At fixed 40 MiB allocation/327,680 aligned 128-byte lines, requesting four/two/one 32-byte portions per line sustains 23.343/38.505/42.802 Glookup/s. At fixed 12 MiB requested data, spreading over 98,304/196,608/393,216 lines changes rate from 43.214/43.207 to 28.119 Glookup/s. Doubling address span at equal data and line count adds a strongest-near-transition penalty. All 1,408 sparse-address and 144 refinement rows validate. Terms describe controlled layouts and timing, not privileged NVIDIA sectors, tags, sets, partitions or TLB events.

claim: Independent sparse packed-LUT full-rate address reach transitions between 252 and 256 MiB on the named workload
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH ADDRESS-MODEL AND COUNTER BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and page-span page-stride plus stride-skew runs
technical_note: At fixed 131,072 useful words/containing test lines, 2,016/2,048/2,080-byte pitch spans 252/256/260 MiB and sustains 42.178/34.318/32.546 Glookup/s globally with texture agreeing at 42.194/34.454/32.778. Exact 4-KiB spacing independently reproduces the 256-MiB loss. Three corpora contain 2,592 valid rows and 656,375,021,568 timed lookups. Timing bounds an address-distribution resource but cannot identify TLB entries, page size, set mapping, partitions or page walks.

claim: Exact power-of-two sparse-LUT pitch can create native texture-path aliasing removable by one 32-byte stride skew
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH INDEX-MODEL AND COUNTER BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four stride-skew runs
technical_note: At target 7 MiB, 992/1,024/1,056-byte pitch gives 42.802/28.621/43.007 Glookup/s through TLD while LDG remains 42.792/42.792/42.807. At target 8 MiB, texture reaches 42.805/26.494/42.775 for 480/512/544-byte pitch. Larger padded layouts outperform the exact power-of-two case, rejecting monotonic span/page-count causation for this component. The result does not declare physical set, bank or partition mapping.

claim: The sparse-LUT 248-256 MiB throughput transition survives with constant 2 MiB physical backing
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH VIRTUAL-ADDRESS AND COUNTER BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four CUDA VMM-alias runs
technical_note: Every virtual slot aliases one 2 MiB device-local allocation while both native paths share the exact mapping. At 1,104 warps global/texture sustain 42.975/42.838 Glookup/s at 240 MiB and fall to 39.523/39.539 at 248 MiB, 35.663/35.687 at 252 MiB and 34.439/34.456 at 256 MiB. Fixed-alias pitch sweeps reproduce the loss. All 368 rows and 77,657,538,560 timed lookups validate. This proves a virtual-address distribution/reach effect for the workload but does not identify hardware page size, TLB entries, page walks, sets or partitions.

claim: CUDA grants an explicitly requested generic-compressible device-local VMM allocation on the named GPU
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH PROPERTY BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and native VMM compression probe
technical_note: The device capability bit is true; request enum 0 returns effective 0 and request enum 1 returns effective 1 through cuMemGetAllocationPropertiesFromHandle. Both 2 MiB handles create, map, accept a complete fill and verify first/last-word readback. The property does not report achieved compression ratio or compressed bytes.

claim: CUDA generic compression adds effective cache capacity to the tested information-bearing periodic or entropy-dense packed6 LUT
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four paired VMM compression-LUT runs
technical_note: Across 4-128 MiB at 1,104 warps, median generic/non-compressible hot-rate ratios are 0.99999/1.00001x for periodic global/texture and 1.00003/1.00005x for entropy-dense global/texture. Both retain the 36-40 MiB cliff. Compression modes coexist and alternate each sample; every handle reports the requested effective property.

claim: CUDA generic compression expands the all-zero packed6 throughput-equivalent allocation capacity through 240 MiB
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH ZERO-ENTROPY AND COUNTER BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four primary plus four zero-span VMM compression runs
technical_note: The generic-compressible global path sustains 38.498-38.650 Glookup/s from 36 through 240 MiB, holding 335,544,320 zero codes versus the 50,331,648-code 36 MiB baseline: a 6.667x throughput-equivalent allocation bound. It falls to 28.823 at 248 MiB and 4.748 at 320 MiB. The separate all-one global control supplies nonzero semantic corroboration. This is not a measured physical compression ratio and zero data carries no useful code information.

claim: CUDA generic compression expands the all-one packed6 throughput-equivalent allocation capacity through 240 MiB
disposition: SUPPORTED ON NAMED DEVICE WITH CONSTANT-CONTENT AND COUNTER BOUNDS
source_basis: Physical GPU report and four all-one global VMM compression runs
technical_note: Every logical code is 63 and every packed word is 0xFFFFFFFF. The generic-compressible global path sustains 38.603-38.652 Glookup/s from 36 through 240 MiB versus 7.004 non-compressible at 240 MiB; it falls to 28.834 at 248 MiB and 5.961 at 320 MiB. All 96 rows and 101,744,640 payloads validate with zero code mismatches. This supports a constant-pattern class, not arbitrary useful-data compression or a physical byte ratio.

claim: The exceptionally fast all-zero texture-object curve is valid decoded-throughput or cache-capacity evidence
source_basis: Physical GPU report plus texture alignment and constant mismatch controls
technical_note: A 174-210 MiB sweep finds an exact three-MiB rate rhythm and one 12-byte group changes rate by up to 19.2x, but all-one texture rows have zero valid timed payloads while all-one global and periodic/entropy texture rows validate. The mismatch probe finds 35,893,872/36,175,872 wrong codes at 4 MiB and 22,609,920/36,175,872 at 192 MiB. A zero expected value masks the failure, so zero-texture rates are excluded from compression and capacity claims.
